title: Tributary message envelope (record projection), v0
description: Validates a JSON projection of one Kafka record: topic class, key, tb-* headers, payload size. See README.md. Strict on the produce side; consumers must not reject unknown headers at runtime.
$comment: The projection carries NO record key value, only its presence and length: the key is usually a patient identifier, and a validator error message embeds the failing instance, which would put PHI into exceptions, logs and test output. The presence and length rules are all the schema ever checked anyway.

class.description: Topic class the record is on. Derivable from 'topic' via the topics contract.

key_present.description: False means the Kafka record key is null (allowed only when the channel declares ordering: none).

key_size.description: Length of the record key in bytes, 0 when null. The key VALUE is deliberately not part of this projection; see the $comment at the root.

payload_present.description: False means the Kafka record value is null.

payload_size.description: Length of the record value in bytes. 0 when the value is null.

allOf.$comment: Claim-check and inline payload are mutually exclusive (README section 5).
Class raw: no destination-, retry- or failure-specific headers.
Class out: destination required, no failure headers yet.
Class retry: a delivery already failed, so the failure context and the delay tier are mandatory.
Class dlq: failing stage and code required; destination only if the failure was at a destination.
Class reply: correlation id is the whole point; tb-source and tb-attempt are optional.

requiredCore.$comment: Headers required on every data-plane class except reply.

headers.description: Kafka headers decoded to UTF-8 text, last value wins. At most 32 entries; the 16 KiB total is a producer-side check, but per-value maxima bound the worst case well inside it.

tb-correlation-id.$comment: UUID only, minted by the engine (ADR-001 6.5). It is the reply-topic record key and reaches _tb.events, ClickHouse and the browser in clear text, so a sender-supplied token that might contain an identifier must be mapped by the receiver, not passed through.

tb-claim-check.$comment: Opaque object locator only. No query string (presigned URLs put credentials there), no fragment, no userinfo (no '@'), no spaces. The object key is derived from non-PHI parts only: <env>/<channel>/<yyyy>/<mm>/<dd>/<tb-msg-id>. Signed URLs are minted at read time by the API and never stored in an envelope or an event.

headers.$comment: Value budget: the 16 KiB total is a producer-side check, but the schema bounds the worst case so open-ended headers cannot blow it. The 16 registered header values sum to about 2.5 KiB, and the 16 remaining slots can only be tb-usr-*/tb-x-* at 256 bytes each, so a schema-valid header set is roughly 7 KiB including names - comfortably inside 16 KiB. The earlier 1024-byte allowance for those two prefixes admitted about 32 KiB, twice the budget.

^tb-x-[a-z0-9-]{1,48}$.$comment: Experimental / spike-local. Never load-bearing. 256 bytes, not 1024: see the header budget $comment above.

^tb-usr-[a-z0-9-]{1,48}$.$comment: Channel-defined. Propagated, never interpreted, and NOT projected into _tb.events in v0. No PHI (invariant 6): a header is readable by anything with topic read access. Must never carry the record key (README section 4).
